Alice — thanks for the clear list and the RFP. Short answer: both paths are viable; which to pick depends on the customer's procurement constraints and priorities. TL;DR recommendations below, then more detail.

TL;DR
- If FinLytics needs to purchase through their marketplace (policy/PO requirement) and wants fastest time-to-use: AWS/GCP/Azure marketplace private offer is usually the fastest route.
- If FinLytics requires negotiated MSA terms, advanced security addenda, or custom billing terms (extended SLA/enterprise support), a direct contract gives more flexibility.

Quick pros/cons (high-level)
- Marketplace (public or private offer):
  - Pros: Faster procurement (PO to license), supports PO/invoice routing in many enterprises, integrates with customer cloud billing, and can be used with private offers to control pricing.
  - Cons: Marketplace platform fees may add to list price or reduce partner margin; some enterprise legal addenda need to be handled outside the marketplace (we typically link MSA via a DocuSign private offer).
- Direct contract / invoice:
  - Pros: Full control over contract language, easier to include custom security addenda, straightforward revenue recognition for us, and simpler to offer volume-based discounts or committed GAUs.
  - Cons: Procurement cycles can be longer (legal + PO), and some customers' finance systems prefer marketplace purchases for cloud software.

Co-sell implications
- Private offers on AWS Marketplace can be co-sell eligible, but co-sell enrollment and capture of partner incentives requires coordination with AWS account team and registration BEFORE purchase.
- Direct deals can also be co-sell if we register with the AWS GTM team and follow their process.

Next steps I propose:
1) Vanessa and I confirm whether FinLytics' purchase must be routed via the marketplace (policy) or if exceptions are allowed.
2) If marketplace is mandatory, we offer a private offer configured for FinLytics (invoice to customer, 12-month term suggested). We'll loop AWS partner ops to confirm co-sell eligibility.
3) If direct, we'll prepare a starter SOW + MSA and fast-track legal review with their team.

Adding operational details from our side — attaching the internal checklist (Redwood_CoSell_Checklist.pdf) to show steps. Key items:

- Marketplace private offer is our recommended default when customers insist on marketplace purchases. We can set up the private offer so FinLytics receives an invoice and Redwood gets paid through AWS (or split depending on marketplace rules).
- For co-sell: to get partner incentives, we need the AWS AE to register the opportunity and the customer to sign the AWS co-sell forms. If the purchase happens via a marketplace public listing (card or subscription), co-sell capture is trickier. Private offers and negotiated offers are fine.
- Legal / security addenda: marketplace purchases do not prevent us from executing an MSA or signing security addenda — we usually execute a side-letter or attach the MSA as part of the private-offer / DocuSign flow. That adds a small amount of administrative work but it's standard.
- Billing terms: most marketplaces support invoice routing/net-30 through private offers; if FinLytics requires custom invoicing fields, direct invoicing is simpler.

Operational recommendation: if policy requires marketplace and procurement can accept a private offer invoice, we do private offer + register the opportunity for co-sell. If their legal insists on specific MSA edits, we route to direct contracting.
